I came to this hospital at 1 PM and ended up waiting in the queue for almost 4 hours. Luckily, my condition wasn’t serious, but I kept thinking—what if someone with a serious problem had to wait this long? What would happen to them, and who would take responsibility?

I really want to request that you improve your management system. Please hire or train staff who can manage patient flow better. As a patient, thisexperience was stressful, and I hope no one else has to go through it in the future.

I would like to explain how patient care is prioritized at this government hospital, especially for foreign patients.

All patients are first assessed by medical staff and classified as clinically stable or unstable, based on basic evaluations such as vital signs.
•	If your vital signs are stable, you will be directed to the Outpatient Department (OPD).
•	If your vital signs are unstable, you will be managed in the Emergency Department (ED).

As this is a government hospital, medical resources and staff are limited. Therefore, priority is given to severe and life-threatening cases, such as patients who are unconscious, require intubation, have severe trauma, or conditions that may result in organ loss.

For this reason, long waiting times—especially at night—are normal, particularly if your condition is stable, such as having cough, fever, or mild symptoms that have already been evaluated by medical staff.

If you prefer faster service, you may choose to visit a private clinic or private hospital. However, please be aware that the cost will be significantly higher compared to government hospitals, which provide more affordable care.

Thank you for your understanding.
Please take good care of yourself—and always wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle.

A very negative experience. This hospital is extremely tourist-oriented and clearly focused on money rather than patient care.

We came in with a kidney stone and were charged around $2,000 just for a CT scan, blood test and urine test. A month later in Bali, we had the same issue again another kidney stone and paid only $400 for a CT scan, blood test, and urine test.

The worst part was the attitude. They refused to give any medication or even basic pain relief until we paid upfront and waited for insurance approval. The patient was in severe pain, vomiting, and feeling terrible, but the staff didn’t seem to care at all.

I strongly do not recommend this hospital. It felt more like a business targeting tourists than a real medical facility.

The nurses will call you by number and name. They will make sure to call in a way you understand if you aren't Thai, so don't worry about language barriers.

The doctors and nurses speak perfectly understandable English. The doctor even filled out my care recommendation in English.

In the winter, a kind man from Switzerland is at the information desk to help you find your way around.

Do note that the nurses have a lunch break ending at about 13:00, with the doctors' break ending at about 13:30, so for non- emergency cases I recommend you come in the morning.

There is a very cute garden smoking area with some animals and a stone table with a chess board on it. If you stand facing the blue atm (pictured) and look to the right you'll see it just next to the ramp.

I hope I don't get injured again (I walked into a low concrete structure lol), but if I do I'll feel safe and happy coming here!

When you are called eventually you are asked if you've taken your blood pressure and had you had your weight & height taken (of course not, no one told us this was required) This was done and we continued to wait for what seemed another hour. It is 1345 now. A short consultation & we were advised to sit outside another area for 'dressing'. We sat outside the dressing area, not knowing to ask or wait ? So I decided to ask and the hospital person said to wait. It is now 1430. at 1500, we had a small dressing cleaned and rebandaged. The hospital prescribed painkillers and antibiotics. That cost 1400 bahtt. We left after paying and picking up the prescription. It's now 1545. We arrived at 0900.

So if you do come here, make sure you register and have your blood pressure and height and weight taken and be prepared for a very long wait. Ideally, bring water and something to snack on.
